editorial:
Imagine living in a quiet flat in San Sebastian where everything seems normal, until you realize your elderly neighbor is watching your every move. You will meet Antonio and Teresa, a young couple just living their lives, and Ursula, a woman in her 70s who has a huge crush on Antonio. She spends her days spying on them from her window, but things get really weird after she catches them in an intimate moment. Instead of feeling bad, she gets an idea that is totally out there. She tells Antonio she is actually pregnant and claims the baby is his, even though they have never even touched. It is a wild setup that blends awkward comedy with a strange kind of drama.

The acting is what really sells this story because you can feel the tension and the confusion in every scene. While the pace is a bit slower than modern movies, the shock value of the lie keeps you interested. It is a great pick if you like stories about obsession and people acting in unpredictable ways. Since this is an older gem, you should try to find it on a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or check if you can rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing how far Ursula is willing to go to keep her lie alive. As the story progresses, you realize she is not actually pregnant, but her obsession with Antonio has completely taken over her mind. The ending reveals the sadness and loneliness behind her actions. She just wanted to feel young and loved again. It ends on a bittersweet note that makes you feel sorry for her even though she lied.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky foreign films and psychological stories.
